center.note: Map centre and anchor of the IceCube coordinate frame; a camera position, not a survey. The ice carries the array about 10 m a year relative to geographic coordinates, so the absolute position is only good to about 500 m. Web Mercator cannot render the South Pole, so the browser draws this map in a local polar azimuthal projection.

levels.name: Ice surface
levels.note: The station and the IceTop tanks sit on the surface of the Antarctic ice sheet, elevation approximately 2,835 m (sourced on facility:amundsen-scott-south-pole-station); the ice sheet, and everything on and in it, drifts about 10 m per year.

name: Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station: IceCube, DeepCore and IceTop
notes: The IceCube coordinate frame is now anchored: the IceCube instrumentation paper (arXiv:1612.05093, version 3 of 6 Feb 2024, section 5.3) states that the y-axis is aligned with the Prime Meridian (Grid North, towards Greenwich) and the x-axis points 90 degrees clockwise (Grid East), and the IceCube repository i3astropy gives the nominal location of the detector centre (lat -89.9944, lon -62.6081, height 883.9 m, the elevation of the frame origin). Earlier worklogs said no source gave the orientation; they had read an older version of the paper (docs.icecube.aq still returns HTTP 401 to every fetch).

Absolute accuracy of the IceCube features is about 500 m (anchor of unstated epoch, ice drift about 10 m a year, and the Wikipedia/OpenStreetMap point for IceCube, 89.99 S 63.4531 W, lies 489 m away); the relative layout of strings and tanks is good to about 1 m and drawn at true size and orientation.

String and tank positions come from the IC86 geometry text file in the IceCube repository icecube/toise (strings) and the GraphNeT copy of the same geometry (IceTop tanks, checked against the IceTop paper); see the worklog docs/atlas-worklog/RELEASE_GEOMETRY_arrays-a.md.
The contract allows no MultiPoint geometry, so string and tank groups are drawn as MultiPolygons of small markers, split to stay within 400 vertices per record.

Overpass (queried 2026-10-25, extract timestamp 2026-10-25T10:37:51Z) holds only the station village node, the ceremonial pole node and the IceCube office node (a copy of the Wikipedia coordinate) near the pole; no IceCube Laboratory building or station building footprint is mapped.

summary.plain: The U.S. research station at the geographic South Pole and the IceCube neutrino telescope beside it. The map shows the 86 in-ice strings (including the dense DeepCore centre) and the 162 IceTop surface tanks at their true spacing, with grid north up; the whole pattern could be shifted by up to about half a kilometre because the ice moves and the published anchor is nominal. ARA, AMANDA, the IceCube Upgrade and IceCube-Gen2 are not drawn.
summary.technical: Local map for facility:amundsen-scott-south-pole-station. IceCube in-ice string positions (strings 1-86) are the mean horizontal positions of each string's DOMs in the IC86 geometry file published in the IceCube repository icecube/toise; IceTop tank positions come from the GraphNeT copy of the same geometry. The IceCube coordinate frame (y along the Prime Meridian, grid north; x grid east) is placed with its origin at the nominal detector location from icecube/i3astropy, in a South Pole azimuthal-equidistant plane. Relative layout about 1 m; absolute placement about 500 m. ARA stations, AMANDA, the IceCube Upgrade strings and IceCube-Gen2 remain unlocated.

unlocated.backlog: Find a table of as-built ARA station coordinates in the South Pole grid or IceCube frame (a station-deployment paper appendix or the collaboration's geometry files); with the frame orientation now sourced, grid offsets convert with the anchor used for IceCube on this map.
unlocated.reason: ARA's five stations (A1-A5) sit about 2 km from the IceCube array, but no source fetched gives their individual coordinates, spacing or bearings. The ARA overview paper (arXiv:2411.01761) states only the ~2 km distance from IceCube, no map or per-station layout. The ARA design paper (arXiv:1105.2854) describes the baseline 37-station, 2 km hexagonal-grid concept (not the five as-built stations) and puts the 2011 testbed 'approximately 1.8 km grid East of the IceCube detector'. The grid orientation is now sourced (IceCube instrumentation paper v3, section 5.3), but an offset of a testbed is not an as-built station position and a web search on 2026-10-25 found no table of A1-A5 coordinates.
